stories.title: Legal aid changes 'unfair, illogical', High Court finds
stories.summary: The High Court has found that new regulations brought in by Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan to govern the payment of legal aid in criminal cases are "grossly unfair" and "demonstrably illogical". The new regulations providing for a flat fee of €520 to be paid per accused person, regardless of the number of charges against them or the number of court appearances, are at the centre of a dispute between the minister and criminal legal aid solicitors which has disrupted the criminal justice system for more than four months. Solicitor John Quinn challenged the new regulations in a judicial review. Mr Quinn, and the solicitors' representative body, the Law Society, who were notice parties to the case, argued the new regulations were unlawful as they provided for the certification and payment of legal aid in a way that went beyond the legislation. In her ruling, Ms Justice Mary Rose Gearty said the provision in the new scheme of a single payment to a solicitor when the final order in the case is made is "grossly unfair". The minister has since tweaked the scheme, allowing for two-thirds of the fee to be paid at the beginning of the case and the remainder at the end of the case or after 12 months.

stories.title: Behind The Story: Strike looms and MV Matthew seizure
stories.summary: Unions have announced plans for a public sector strike on Thursday 12 November over delays in agreeing a new pay deal. Despite hopes of a breakthrough last week, the talks were abruptly adjourned without agreement on Friday night, with unions saying the government had made no credible offer on pay. "Union lead negotiator Kevin Callinan said if they didn't have a credible offer by the end of the weekend, then they would have no choice but to escalate their industrial action. So fast forward to today, Monday, and that's exactly what happened." Despite the break down Brian explains the situation is not intractable. "What is going to happen next is that tomorrow the trade unions are actually going to meet with a government appointed group that's been set up to try to bring the sides back together." The strike could also disrupt preparations for a key meeting of European leaders in Dublin due to take place on 12-13 November as part of Ireland's EU presidency.

stories.title: Apple forecasts margin drop as rising memory costs bite
stories.summary: Apple has warned that the cost of memory chips would continue to rise, pressuring gross margin for the crucial Christmas quarter, but said it had taken steps to lock in supplies. Shares, little changed in after-hours trading after fiscal fourth-quarter results beat expectations, fell 4% during a conference call after executives outlined the weaker outlook, but later pared losses to a 2% decline. Early demand for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and higher prices boosted the quarter. Apple said it expects gross margin of 45% to 46% in the quarter ending in December, down from 47.9% in the fourth quarter. It forecast services revenue growth of 8% to 9%, below analysts' expectations of 10.7%. The results come as Apple experiments with a string of firsts under new CEO John Ternus, who took over in September. After nearly two decades of launching most new iPhones each autumn, Apple this year is spacing them out, with iPhone Pro and Duo models shipping this year and other models expected next year. Apple also released a bevy of new non-iPhone products this quarter, including its first touchscreen laptops and first smart-home hub. The steady drumbeat of releases, analysts said, is meant to smooth out Apple's yearly revenue cycle, which for decades showed a huge holiday-quarter boom that petered out by late summer.

stories.title: What you need to know about the 2026 US midterm elections
stories.summary: Early voting has been under way for weeks ahead of the midterm elections, when US voters will elect members of the House of Representatives and Senate and governors in states across the country. Held in the middle of each four-year presidential term, the midterms by definition do not involve the president. However, for anyone who thinks they lack drama or importance this year, consider these two statistics: More than 57 million people had already cast their ballots as of Monday, according to the University of Florida Election Lab, well above the 46 million who voted early in the 2022 midterm elections. This election is on track to be the most expensive in US history. The nonpartisan watchdog OpenSecrets estimates a total of $11.9 billion will be spent by candidates and outside political groups. Elon Musk alone had spent about $366 million to support Republicans as of three weeks ago, according to campaign finance records.

stories.title: Point of Law wins Melbourne Cup as Maher sweeps top three
stories.summary: Point Of Law won the Melbourne Gold Cup as Australian trainer Ciaron Maher saddled the first three home. Sons And Lovers was the first of Joseph O'Brien’s five-strong contingent to finish, coming home in fourth place. James J Braddock finished back in seventh place, as Maher claimed the other five slots in the top seven, Having claimed the Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket in July for John and Thady Gosden in the colours of the King and Queen, Point Of Law was bought privately by Wathnan Racing. In winning the Geelong Cup on his first start for Maher, he was immediately promoted to favouritism and came in at 11/2 with Ethan Brown on board. Point Of Law was made to work for victory by Royal Supremacy, who at one stage led by 15 lengths before fading in the final furlong.

stories.title: All you need to know about why Godzilla has endured for so long
stories.summary: Analysis: Cinema's greatest monster has been on the loose for 72 years and has been reimagined, reinvented and changed in dramatic ways during this period It's Godzilla Day, the annual celebration spearheaded by the Japanese film studio (and owners of the Godzilla film franchise) Toho. It's 72 years since the release of Ishiro Honda's original Godzilla film and Godzilla Day 2026 will see the release of the latest Godzilla film, Godzilla Minus Zero. The film is the 39th in the long-running franchise and reunites the titular monster with director Takashi Yamazaki, who previously helmed 2023’s Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One. Next year will see the release of Grant Sputore’s Godzilla Supernova, a continuation of the American Monsterverse series (think the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but swap out Captain America and Iron Man for Godzilla and King Kong). The Japanese Godzilla films are usually sorted into four main categories or 'eras’: the Showa era, the Heisei era, the Millennium era and the Reiwa era (the first, second and fourth eras refer to the reigns of successive Japanese emperors that overlap with release dates). In each era, the monster has found itself reimagined and reinvented, changing in dramatic ways. These reinventions are why Godzilla has endured so well – the monster is adaptable and is consistently used to respond to (or metaphorically depict) major historical and political events. Here are some of the notable roles Godzilla has served over the past seven decades. The very first Godzilla is a strange film. The monster now has a reputation as the star of entertainingly bizarre and often funny action films. Little of this exuberance is to be found in Ishiro Honda’s stark 1954 masterpiece, which is a bleak, fantastical reckoning with post-war life in 1950s Japan. Characters make casual, desultory reference to the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, while continuing atomic tests in the South Pacific hang over proceedings (Godzilla is implied to have been awoken by tests near Bikini Atoll). The 1954 case of the Lucky Dragon fishing vessel – where the crew suffered radiation poisoning, social alienation and death as a result of nuclear tests – served as an inspiration for both the monster and its victims. In one dark scene, after Godzilla has levelled Tokyo, scientists scan children at an abandoned school with a Geiger counter. They shake their heads in sadness as the results, offscreen, indicate severe poisoning.

stories.title: John Malkovich: 'Nobody liked my Irish accent!'
stories.summary: Actor John Malkovich has joked about how his attempt at an Irish accent in his new movie Wild Horse Nine fell flat with Irish members of the film crew and director Martin McDonagh. Set shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, the film by the In Bruges and Banshees of Inisherin writer and film maker sees Malkovich play Chris Carlisle, a jaded CIA agent who takes a break from destabilising the Chilean government and is dispatched to Easter Island with his partner Lee Chesterfield (Sam Rockwell). This odd couple spend most of the time driving around in a battered old coupe (the coup comes later) and bickering as they visit the island's famous monolithic statues while discussing the nature of the dirty work they carry out on behalf of the US government. Chris, who is also riddled with Catholic guilt and terminal cancer, is seeking to salve his conscious after a lifetime of covert activity by writing his tell-all memoirs. As he says to Lee at one point, "I was killing people before you were born." Meanwhile, back in the Chilean capital of Santiago, Steve Buscemi as bureau chief MJ is slowly losing his mind as he worries that lose cannon Chris is about to betray everyone. It’s classic McDonagh stuff. Quirky and absurd, what seems like a classic shaggy dog story sees the Anglo-Irish director riff on recurrent themes such as stunted morality, guilt, redemption, and men’s basic inability to communicate with each other.

stories.title: West Cork couple tie the knot in surprise wedding on US chat show
stories.summary: Most couple's nuptials are presided over by a parish priest or maybe even a close friend or relative, but for one West Cork couple, theirs was led by none other than an Oscar-winning star. Amanda Murnane and Brendan Hayes, a couple from Bantry, became the first couple to wed on The Jennifer Hudson Show last month, in a surprise ceremony that was officiated by the bubbly host herself. The couple have a long love story, having been together for 27 years and sharing three children, Rene, Clarice and Michael, and one grandson, Wayne. Both have spent years working for West Cork Mental Health Services, while Brendan is also an independent filmmaker, documentary maker, writer, actor and director. Although they had long wanted to get married, a number of obstacles held them back, most notably in 2011 when their daughter Rene was diagnosed with leukemia. While Rene eventually overcame that health setback, that period of their lives was marked by stress and difficulty, which led Brendan to wanting to give Amanda something positive. Their story got another cinematic twist on 23 October when Brendan surprised Amanda with an elaborately planned wedding on stage, in front of a live studio audience. The plan was hatched over months, with Brendan secretly arranging the surprise alongside the show's production team.

stories.title: Polls open on east coast in pivotal US midterm elections
stories.summary: Polls have opened on the US east coast as Americans are set to deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's second presidency in midterm elections. Democrats are hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Mr Trump. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Mr Trump's legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials. The election amounts to a nationwide judgement on Mr Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war against Iran. All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

stories.title: Primark-Penneys owner forecasts further profit decline
stories.summary: Associated British Foods has today forecast another year of lower profits after reporting a 14% fall in earnings for 2025/26, pressured by deepening losses in its sugar business and lower underlying sales at its Primark/Penneys fashion chain. The FTSE 100 group, which plans to demerge Primark from its food businesses next year, said it remained cautious on consumer sentiment as well as the impact of inflation and higher energy costs on its businesses. It said adjusted operating profit in the year to September 2027 would be below the £1.51 billion reported in 2025/26, largely due to sugar losses that could widen to as much as £170m. "Any consumer facing business is trading with the reality of consumers whose spending power is reduced," CEO George Weston told Reuters. Shares in the group were down 3.1%, extending losses this year to 11.5%. AB Foods said work on the demerger was progressing well and remained on track for completion in December 2027.

stories.title: Ireland to face world champs Spain in Nations League A
stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland women's side will face world champions Spain as well as Norway and Switzerland in League A of the upcoming UEFA Nations League, following Tuesday's draw. The headline clash against Spain marks the first meeting between the two nations in over a decade; their last encounter came in April 2016, when Spain secured a 3-0 victory in UEFA Women’s EURO 2017 qualifying. Reflecting on the draw, Republic of Ireland head coach Carla Ward quipped: "Who doesn't want to play against the world champions? "From the moment I took this job, I’ve said time and time again that we want to test ourselves against the very best, and this is our opportunity. Spain are the best team in the world right now; their quality is exceptional and nobody really comes close to them. "We know the challenge ahead. It’s going to be a game where we have to be extraordinarily disciplined, stay compact, and frustrate them. We’ve shown against sides like France and the Netherlands that we have that resilience in our DNA, and that has to be the exact mindset we bring to the pitch. Ward also added: "There are no easy games at this level in League A. Norway have real prestige as former world champions, and on paper they possess one of the strongest squads in world football. They're also managed by a good friend of mine in Gemma Grainger, so I'm really looking forward to going up against her.

stories.title: Andrew Scott-starring Elsinore leads BIFA nominations
stories.summary: The Andrew Scott-starring Elsinore leads the shortlist for this year's British Independent Film Awards (BIFA) with 12 nominations. Among Elsinore's nominations are Best Lead Performance for Scott, Best Supporting Performance for Billie Piper, Best British Independent Film, Best Director for Simon Stone, and Best Screenplay for Simon Beresford. The biographical drama stars Scott as the late Scottish actor Ian Charleson as he prepares to play Hamlet at the National Theatre in London while seriously ill with AIDS. Elsinore is tipped to be among next year's Oscar nominees in multiple categories. Scott previously won Best Supporting Actor at the British Independent Film Awards for his performance in Pride. Other nominations of Irish interest on this year's BIFA shortlist are Enda Walsh in the Best Screenplay category for I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, Daryl McCormack and Lola Petticrew in the Best Ensemble Performance category for I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, and Clare Dunne in the Best Joint Lead Performance category for The Education of Jane Cumming.

stories.title: 8 household jobs to tackle in November
stories.summary: Although it might feel too early to put up your Christmas tree, there are plenty of cleaning jobs to tick off this November before the festivities start to ramp up. Here are eight household chores to tackle now during the quieter season before the fast-approaching holiday rush begins… It’s common to forget about the freezer until you are confronted with overflowing shelves of mystery food just before Christmas. "Go into the freezer and have a proper clear-out before all the Christmas food starts to arrive," recommends cleaning and organising expert and Sunday Times bestselling author Gemma Bray, also known as The Organised Mum. She suggests getting creative with your meal planning to clear out as much freezer food as possible before Christmas. "This will help you save money [on food] that you can repurpose towards your Christmas budget, and will also free up room in the freezer for all of the festive goodies that will come in," explains Bray.

stories.title: Hoax bomb threats disrupt at least four flights in Europe
stories.summary: At least four European flights have been targeted by bomb threats, forcing the temporary closure of one Warsaw airport, but all planes landed safely and no explosives were found, authorities said. Two bomb warnings targeted flights heading to the Polish capital Warsaw, including an SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen and one from London's Heathrow airport operated by Polish airline LOT. In a third incident Aena, the Spanish airport operator, confirmed an emergency protocol was activated "due to a bomb alert" on a Ryanair flight from the northwestern UK city of Manchester to Murcia in southeastern Spain. A Wizz Air flight from Bergamo, Italy, was inspected after landing at 09.10am in the Bulgarian capital Sofia, a Bulgarian interior ministry spokesperson said. The incidents come after fighter jets were scrambled yesterday when a Wizz Air flight from London's Luton airport to Sofia was diverted following a bomb threat and forced to make an emergency stop in Budapest. Today's Ryanair flight landed without incident in Murcia, and the emergency plan was deactivated after checks by Spain's Civil Guard.

stories.title: Beshoffs gave EU staff better pay and hours - claim
stories.summary: A Turkish worker has said she was discriminated against and made to feel like "rubbish" when her bosses at the Beshoffs fish and chips chain refused the annual leave she sought for her own wedding. The employee, Zerha Fidan, has accused Beshoff Brothers operating company Glendalon Ltd of giving EU nationals better pay, preferential shift allocations and priority for annual leave, in breach of the Employment Equality Act 1998. She told the Workplace Relations Commission she could not quit her job as a counter assistant at its restaurant in Clontarf, Dublin 3, even after being denied leave for the wedding - because her residency entitlements in Ireland were tied to her employment. Her lawyers argue she was discriminated against on the grounds of race in breach of the Employment Equality Act, a claim being disputed by the restaurant group at the WRC. Ms Fidan started work at Beshoffs in November 2022, shortly after arriving to Ireland, and worked at various locations before being sent to work at its Clontarf restaurant, she told the WRC last week. Ms Fidan's evidence was that when the National Minimum Wage was raised to €12.70 at the start of 2024, she was kept on this rate until August that year, despite two colleagues - both EU nationals - at the shop getting a higher hourly rate.

stories.title: Mourners told Mageean was an 'inspirational human being'
stories.summary: Mourners at the funeral of Irish Olympian and European champion Ciara Mageean have been told she was a bright light in the darkness who made the world a nicer place to call home. Hundreds of people packed into St Patrick's Church, just a few hundred metres along the road from her home in Portaferry in Co Down, with many more standing outside. There was a guard of honour by members of her local Portaferry GAA club, where she took her first sporting steps playing camogie. President Catherine Connolly and the Taoiseach were represented by their aides-de-camp, and Sinn Féin deputy leader and Northern Ireland’s First Minister Michelle O’Neill attended the service. Well known figures from the world of sport, including Irish Olympians and GAA President Jarlath Burns were also present. Many others watched a livestream of the service from across the world.

stories.title: Rovers' O'Neill: Cancer doesn't pick and choose
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers' Gary O'Neill, who was diagnosed with cancer in October of 2025 and got the all clear earlier this year, has encouraged people to go for regular check-ups in light of his own diagnosis and the recent passing of Ciara Mageean. "When I got diagnosed in October, I tried to keep things as private as I possibly could and deal with whatever was going to come with just me and my family. I didn't really want it to get out. I didn't want the sympathy from people," he said. "It was just about facing my battle with the people I wanted to face the battle with. Then when I got the news that my cancer was shrinking and the treatment was working I became more open to the idea of potentially having a conversation about it. "I thought it was just a really important message for me to spread because I was fit, I was healthy, 29/30 years of age and trained every day. Looked after myself the best I can and I had an 18cm tumor in my stomach when I found the cancer. So, it doesn't pick and choose. It's something that was heavy and if it could have helped one person me opening up my story then I think it's a great success. "My message is and always has been that if something feels off, even if you feel as healthy as you can, there's no repercussions of going to get a blood test. Just go and get yourself checked if you haven't in a while. It's worthwhile just going and doing it now and staying on top of things. These things can be caught early and it makes all the difference." O'Neill added that since receiving his diagnosis and going through treatment, his perspective on things has changed a lot.

stories.title: Scarlett Faulkner struck with 'brutal force', trial told
stories.summary: A jury in the trial of a woman and teenage girl accused of murdering Scarlett Faulkner in Co Tipperary last March has been told she was "hunted down" and struck with "brutal and ferocious force" with a metal pole. The 29-year-old died on 13 April after an incident at Birdhill in Co Tipperary on 21 March last. In his opening statement, prosecuting counsel Seoirse Ó Dúnlaing said the two accused women had acted in a joint enterprise to find and harm Ms Faulkner after discovering she had begun a relationship with an ex partner of the older accused. He told the jury it would hear evidence that the vehicle in which Ms Faulkner was travelling on 13 April had been rammed off the road at Birdhill before she was struck 10 to 11 times with a metal pole by the 17-year-old accused. He said dashcam and other mobile phone footage would show Ms Faulkner being hit with the metal bar by the younger accused before the older woman approached and brought her co-accused back to their vehicle. Mr Ó Dúnlaing said the jury would hear evidence that the older woman had begun looking for Ms Faulkner the previous night and had sent Ms Faulkner’s sister a text message saying: "Your smell bag of a sister will pay for what she done when I get her I’ll draw a map of Ireland on her face."

stories.summary: Injury issues mean we will see changes in Andy Farrell's team selection for Ireland's Nations Championship test against Argentina on Friday night at Aviva Stadium. Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley remain out, Jack Conan has been added to the injury list after sustaining a shoulder injury with Leinster, and Garry Ringrose is the latest key player to join the list of absentees, leaving Farrell with some important selection decisions. These calls may also give some insight into the longer-term strategy for the team. Leinster centre Ringrose's unavailability is one of the major talking points, particularly when it comes to deciding who will fill the gap in midfield. Bundee Aki and Robbie Henshaw have both played there in the past, but if Farrell wants to establish a more permanent position for Jamie Osborne, Ringrose’s absence could provide another opportunity to develop Ireland’s options at centre. Jamie Benson would be more surprising selection at outside centre, though he has featured there for Ulster. He could provide another playmaking option and help to increase the pace of the attacking game.

stories.title: Ó Snodaigh asks to give Dáil statement over charity
stories.summary: Sinn Féin TD Aengus Ó Snodaigh has asked to give a personal statement to the Dáil over the Liberty Recycling controversy. Mr Ó Snodaigh is the chair of the charity, which is under investigation for money laundering. The High Court heard last week that he had signed off on the establishment of two other related entities, which were not charities. The request to Ceann Comhairle Verona Murphy was confirmed by the party this morning, and comes after Tánaiste and Fine Gael leader Simon Harris, among others, called on Mr Ó Snodaigh to outline his position in the Dáil. Speaking to reporters on the plinth at Leinster House, Sinn Féin TD David Cullinane said that while his party "is not going to respond to the Tánaiste", he wanted to confirm that "Aengus has asked to make a statement, which is his right". He said Mr Ó Snodaigh is not under investigation, has already said he is making himself available to help gardaí and the Charities Regulator with their inquiries, and that his party colleague wants the matter resolved as much as anybody.

stories.title: Tipperary's Kennedy announces inter-county retirement
stories.summary: Tipperary senior hurler and three-time All Ireland winner Séamus Kennedy has announced his retirement from inter-county hurling. The 33-year-old spent enjoyed 11 years with the Premier hurlers, with the St Mary's and Clonmel Commercials clubman playing an important role in the county’s All-Ireland wins in 2016, 2019 and 2025. Currently, he is helping St Mary’s hunt a Munster intermediate hurling crown, just weeks after losing a Tipp senior football final with Clonmel Commercials. "The time is right for me to retire from intercounty hurling," he said. "Wearing the blue and gold jersey was a dream come true and I feel very fortunate to have had the opportunity to do so." Tipperary GAA added their appreciation for Kennedy’s outstanding commitment and dedication to the blue and gold jersey across both codes.

stories.title: Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel dies after on-field collision
stories.summary: Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club have announced. The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge 30-year-old striker De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second tier game. The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: "Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda. "There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness. "We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones…that today weep for this cruel outcome. The family of Jesus de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments." Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as "stable despite the severity of his condition".

stories.title: African translator gives evidence in murder trial
stories.summary: A translator of the African language 'Hausa' has given evidence in the trial of a man accused of murdering a pensioner in Co Tipperary two years ago. Hasan Ali Gori, originally from Chad, has pleaded not guilty to murdering Josephine ‘Josie’ Ray in the bedroom of her home in Nenagh on 4 August 2024. The jury at the Central Criminal Court heard evidence last week that Mr Gori told Josie Ray’s daughter to "murder her". The alleged comment was heard on audio recorded on the accused's phone on the night before the alleged killing. The accused was living in the home of the 89-year-old in St Joseph's Park, Nenagh, as he was in a relationship with her daughter, Mary Ray, who has an intellectual disability. The jury of nine men and three women was played extracts of an audio recording found on the phone of Mr Gori during the murder investigation.

stories.title: UK and EU reach draft agreement on food trade - report
stories.summary: Britain and the European Union are reported to have reached a draft agreement on the trade in food and agriculture. If finalised, it would replace the current post-Brexit arrangements that see British food and agriculture exports to the EU subject to costly veterinary and customs checks. The move would have particular significance for Northern Ireland, reducing the impact of the so-called Irish sea border that has existed since Britain left the European Union. It would also significantly impact the food and agriculture trade for the whole of Ireland, which has changed substantially as a result of Brexit. Ireland is the number one market for British food and drink exports. The BBC reported that the UK and the European Commission have reached a draft agreement on sanitary and phytosanitary arrangements that would see the EU drop most of its controls on British food and drink exports in return for the British agreeing to follow EU laws and regulations on food and agriculture production.

stories.title: Concern over lack of special care bed for troubled boy
stories.summary: No special care bed is available for a boy who vomited up almost 40 bags of crack cocaine, the High Court has heard. The boy, who is using fentanyl, is now missing. His case was before the High Court yesterday and was reported in the Irish Times. The court heard there was no special care bed available for him, nor were beds available for two teenage girls, one of them aged just 14, who were being abused by multiple men. The special care service is supposed to provide secure intervention for young people with extremely troubled lives, but because of staff shortages, just 13 of its 26 beds are currently available. "These are really tough cases to read about, especially when you see that these are really vulnerable children," she said. "When you read about this particular case, this young boy who has been through so much and to know now that he's still missing... I'm really concerned about both his safety and welfare but also the fact that we're seeing these cases over and over again and the bigger issues they are pointed to within our child protection system that we need to fix."

stories.title: Russia confirms Ukraine-US talks in Abu Dhabi next week
stories.summary: Russia has confirmed that US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks to end more than four years of war will take place in Abu Dhabi next week. US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff earlier announced the meeting will take place on 10-11 November. Mr Witkoff met with both Russia's Vladimir Putin and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky last month, with all sides announcing three-way talks would resume this month. "The Russian delegation will arrive on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi to take part in trilateral talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. The Russian delegation will be led by Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who took part in previous negotiations that failed to reach a breakthrough. Mr Medinsky is known for his nationalistic views on Russian history.

The Clare native will be returning to the Irish province having previously worked with the club in several roles, including academy manager and Leinster 'A’ head coach during a five-year spell between 2016 and 2021. He also coached the Ireland Under 20s to a Grand Slam in 2019 before spending two years in Durban with the Sharks as their attack and backs coach prior to joining Bordeaux. McNamara will remain in his position with Bordeaux for the remainder of the 2026/27 season before taking up his new role with Leinster on 1 July 2027. "I am delighted that I am returning to Leinster Rugby as head coach in 2027," McNamara said. "This is one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby and it is an honour to be given this responsibility.

stories.title: Coleman 'still thinking about' staying on with Ireland
stories.summary: Séamus Coleman is still keeping the door open on a return to action at club and international level. The 38-year-old, currently without a club, was not included in Heimir Hallgrimsson's UEFA Nations League squad for the quartet of matches in September and October. The indications at the time were that Coleman was on the lookout for a new club in order to prolong his chances of being involved at Euro 2028. Hallgrimsson has shared how keen he is on keeping Coleman in his plans. However the former Everton captain's comments in recent weeks have cast doubt on that possibility. Last week in conversation with Jamie Carragher on the The Overlap Fan Debate, Coleman hinted that he was leaning towards retirement, saying: "I don't want to completely draw a line in the sand, as I said I've been keeping fit. But it's edging towards that way - and happily as well." On Monday, Coleman appeared as a pundit for Sky Sports' coverage of Newcastle United v Everton with speculation rife that he was about to confirm his retirement. Instead, he underlined his stance that nothing has been decided.
